page.layout: Running head at top centre; page number at top left. One column of text: a verse poem at the top, a centred capitals heading, an epigram with a large initial, a short centred line, a two-line italic epigram, the author's initials, and a printed ornament. Catchword at the lower right.

l.i: Aspice uti solitum posuit maris unda furorem,
Aspice uti pauidus flumina tranat Anas,
Aspice uti patrio remeat peregrina solo grus,
Atráq; sol clara nubila luce fugat. T-
um campis humana nitent opera atque labores,
Et noua pinguescens gramina fundit humus.
Quæque parit pulcris fœtum cum floribus arbos,
Omnibus in ramis omnibus in foliis.
Iure quidem dici Dominū te, Auguste, vetabas:
Maior eo Dominus tempore natus erat.
Define,cur videat nemo sine Numine Numen

page.notes: The initial "I" of the epigram is a large letter joined to "re" ("Iure"). Two marks before "Anas" and "Atráq;" are printed ornaments/flourishes and are not transcribed. The printed fleuron below the epigram is an ornament, not text. "Atráq;" has an accent over the a as printed. The "terræ" and "Quæque" ligatures are read from the scan and may be slightly uncertain.
